title: The golden check misses its bar by one row, so the underlines stay off
subtitle: Lomem's gate for the new grading prompt. The two misses in step 4 are an example.

steps.label: skip exact matches to the key
old verdict; new verdict + underlines, timed
real rows: old vs new verdict

outcome.title: FAIL: the underlines stay off
lines: The golden check needs 95% right and got 34 of 36. The bar was set before the run, so the prompt is fixed, never the bar.

captions.title: Load real rows and golden rows
captions.text: Up to 200 real rows come from the staging database, with no person's label. 36 golden rows carry a person's verdict and a note. Answers that exactly match the answer key are skipped, as in production.

captions.title: Run the old and the new prompt on every row
captions.text: Two paid calls per row: up to 236 × 2, about 470 per run. The model picks words with some randomness, so a row can come back different tomorrow.

captions.title: Score real rows against the old verdict
captions.text: Real rows have no human label, so the old verdict is the reference and agreement shows change only. Each disagreement is a break or a fix. A person reads each one.

captions.title: Score golden rows against the person's verdict
captions.text: The golden check needs 95% right and no paraphrase graded wrong. 34 of 36 are right, just under the bar. The misses print with their notes, here "negation lost" and "article error" (example).

captions.title: Keep each quality as its own check
captions.text: Underlines: 95% of replies must put one on a word the learner wrote, and no underlines is a pass. Speed: 95% of new replies within 2.5 seconds. Both checks are plain code.

captions.title: A person reads the misses and fixes the prompt
captions.text: The script prints PASS or FAIL per check and exits normally either way. The golden check failed, so `TD_JUDGE_MARKS` stays off. The bar is never lowered after a miss.
